rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes thermal aging at ~600°C and ~750°C on an as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA, whereas the paper anneals Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 at 1100–1300°C and water-quenches. The material system, initial state, and thermal treatment are entirely different.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis uses aging at 550–750°C to study embrittlement/recovery, while the paper uses high-temperature annealing (1100–1300°C) under argon followed by water quenching to study phase stability and hardness. The temperature regimes and objectives are unrelated.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes L12 ordering, jagged B2/FCC boundaries, and planar slip leading to embrittlement. The paper describes spinodal decomposition into BCC1/BCC2, ordering to B2, and reciprocal BCC/B2 microstructures that increase hardness. The mechanisms are fundamentally different.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts a non-monotonic ductile-brittle-ductile transition with minimized ductility at 600°C. The paper predicts and observes a monotonic increase in hardness with higher annealing/quench temperature. The predicted properties and trends are completely different.
